items.title: Lampard: VAR didn't do its job
items.excerpt: Coventry boss Frank Lampard says VAR 'didn't do its job' in his side's defeat to Everton as three reviews controversially went against his side.
body: Coventry boss Frank Lampard says VAR 'didn't do its job' in his side's defeat to Everton as three reviews controversially went against his side.

Two penalty appeals and a possible handball for Everton's second goal were all reviewed by VAR officials Timothy Wood and Gary Beswick, but nothing was given. They were also not awarded on-field by referee Stuart Attwell.
Coventry opened the scoring after the two penalty appeals, but were ultimately beaten 3-1 on Merseyside on Friday Night Football.

Lampard told Sky Sports: "I hate to sound like a moaner. It's a football match and if you win the game, that can happen here. I've worked here and know the momentum swings in the game. items.title: Jobe joins brother Jude with England to showcase his own talent
items.excerpt: "He's coming on his own merit," said Thomas Tuchel, after extolling the strengths of Jobe Bellingham.
body: "He's coming on his own merit," said Thomas Tuchel, after extolling the strengths of Jobe Bellingham.

Jude Bellingham's younger brother - as is currently the go-to preface to any description of Jobe - couldn't hide his delight when he got the call from Tuchel to say he was being promoted from U21s captain to be included in the England senior squad.

"It's an incredible achievement for the family, for both brothers to be called up by their national team," Tuchel said on Friday, after revealing his squad for the Nations League games with Croatia and Spain. "I saw his excitement straightaway in his smile."

But Tuchel was also right to highlight the individual qualities of 21-year-old Jobe and the different attributes he can offer the national team, in a different position to his brother. items.title: Is Hemp the best winger in the game right now?
items.excerpt: Sky Sports columnist Laura Hunter analyses the big talking points from the sixth round of Women's Super League matches, bringing you closer to the key stories at the heart of the women's game. Why Hemp's form deserves more credit
body: Sky Sports columnist Laura Hunter analyses the big talking points from the sixth round of Women's Super League matches, bringing you closer to the key stories at the heart of the women's game. Why Hemp's form deserves more credit

Plenty of Manchester City's squad featured prominently in the women's Ballon d'Or final rankings last week. Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw rightly came third. Yui Hasegawa finished 11th, while Alex Greenwood and Kerstin Casparij were both named in the top 30. All such placings were a fair reflection of their current status.

But there was one glowing omission. Lauren Hemp, arguably the most in-form winger in the game right now, was curiously nowhere to be seen. It felt odd. And prompted a deeper dive into why she might have been overlooked.

Clearly Bunny Shaw is the undisputed champion of Man City's team, their top scorer and main driver of big results. Incidentally, the Jamaica international is currently on her best run of consecutive scoring starts in the league (8) and has found the net in 13 of 19 games in 2026. items.title: Barcola: People are starting to understand me better - but I'm not Mo Salah
items.excerpt: Big money signings can take time to get going at their new club. There are plenty at Liverpool who can testify to that.
body: Big money signings can take time to get going at their new club. There are plenty at Liverpool who can testify to that.

As Sky Sports settles into a room at Liverpool's AXA training facility, a large window shows some of their big-money stars walking off one of the pitches after a recovery session. It's a sheer amount of attacking wealth.

Two of them are Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who arrived in deals that could reach a combined £241m. But the jury is still out on both of them. Isak has only just started delivering his highly-anticipated goal numbers, while many believe Wirtz is yet to get going on Merseyside.

This year, Bradley Barcola - who goes from the pitch to sitting in front of the Sky Sports cameras in the training facility - is the latest marquee signing, this time for £123m. But a slow start to life at Anfield brought about familiar concerns about recent buys.
